title: PLT jurisdiction keyword filter list
description: Curated linguistic filter used as stage 1 of the PLT ingestion filter chain. One file per jurisdiction. See docs/core-document.md section 2.5.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the file conforms to.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction code. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 for states; 'EU' for the European Union, which is treated as its own jurisdiction.

list_version.description: Semantic version of this list. Bump the minor version when terms are added, the major version when scoring semantics change.

updated.description: ISO 8601 date the list was last curated.

maintainer.description: Role or person responsible for curating this list. Curation is a content-manager responsibility.

languages.description: ISO 639-1 codes of the languages covered. Must cover every working language of the jurisdiction's courts.

notes.description: Free-text curation notes: known gaps, precision/recall observations, decisions taken.

min_score.description: Total weight a document must reach to pass the filter. A single weight-3 term is intended to be sufficient on its own.

review_band.description: Width, in score points above min_score, of the band within which a passing document is additionally flagged for content-manager review. A document scoring min_score <= score < min_score + review_band is ingested and published exactly like any other and placed in the review queue (core document 2.7). Set it per jurisdiction from that jurisdiction's own dry run; 0 disables flagging. Defaults to 3.

count_term_once.description: If true, repeated occurrences of the same term contribute their weight only once.

fields.description: Per-field multipliers applied to a term's weight depending on where it matched.

exclusions.description: Patterns that veto a document outright regardless of score. Use sparingly, for known homonym traps.

id.description: Stable identifier, prefixed with the language code. Never reuse an id for a different term; match provenance is stored against it.

term.description: The term as it appears in court documents, in the source language.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 code of the language this term is written in.

category.description: Used for reporting on which kinds of terms drive recall, and for tuning.

weight.description: 3 = unambiguous, qualifies a document alone. 2 = strong but needs light corroboration. 1 = contextual, only meaningful in combination.

match.description: 'word' matches on word boundaries; 'phrase' matches a whitespace-normalised multi-word sequence; 'substring' matches anywhere (use for compounding languages); 'regex' for the rare case the others cannot express.

case_sensitive.description: Set true only for short acronyms whose lowercase form is a common word. Inherited by every alias, so a case_sensitive term carries acronyms only: an ordinary word that inherits it matches solely the casing curated here.

case_sensitive_exception.description: Opts this term out of the acronym-only rule enforced on case_sensitive terms. Set it only where splitting the ordinary word into its own term would change scoring rather than only structure, accepting that every casing but the curated one scores zero. The loader rejects it on a term that is not case_sensitive, and on one that does not need it. See data/keywords/README.md, 'Known exceptions'.

aliases.description: Spelling variants, inflections and abbreviations that score identically to the term.

requires.description: Term ids that must also match before this term contributes any weight. Use to disarm homonyms.
